scope: Primary arXiv abstract pages and version histories reviewed by the operator for AgentSpec, Progent, and CaMeL. Remaining bibliography identifiers were checked on 12 September 2026 as recorded in primary-source-verification.json. This verifies metadata and bounded descriptions, not implementation behavior, reported scores, or experimental execution.

sources.title: AgentSpec: Customizable Runtime Enforcement for Safe and Reliable LLM Agents
sources.bounded_description: A rule language expresses triggers, predicates and runtime enforcement for agents. Its reported domains include code execution.
sources.review_implication: Runtime constraints and enforcement already have direct agent-system precedents; do not claim the first runtime rule layer.

sources.title: Progent: Securing AI Agents with Privilege Control
sources.bounded_description: Symbolic policies constrain tool names and arguments. The current abstract describes SMT classification of policy updates, with automatic narrowing and approval for expansion.
sources.review_implication: Compare this explicit privilege boundary and security/utility measurement; do not imply that agent policy enforcement or guarded updates are unique to the law-to-action paper.

sources.title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
sources.bounded_description: A layer separates control and data flow from trusted queries and uses capabilities to constrain data flow at tool calls.
sources.review_implication: Discuss this adjacent capability boundary; citations are not evidence that its implementation was benchmarked in this paper.
